argument: In knowledge-intensive projects with tightly coupled tasks, adding staff introduces onboarding, communication, coordination, and integration costs. When the remaining work is not easily partitioned and the deadline is near, these costs can exceed the added productive capacity.
boundary: The effect depends on task divisibility, team maturity, documentation, modularity, and time horizon.
Adding experienced people to independent bottlenecks can help.
The law is not a reason to maintain chronic understaffing.
